items.a: Couples counselling takes place online by video, so you can meet from wherever you are. Sessions offer a calm, balanced space where both of you can speak openly and feel heard, with me supporting the conversation between you. We look at the patterns in your relationship and work towards better understanding, connection, and communication — you can read more about [navigating distance and reconnecting as a couple](/blog/growing-apart-growing-together). Everything happens at a pace that feels safe and respectful for you both.

items.q: Do both partners need to attend?
items.a: Both partners usually attend together, since much of the value comes from the conversation that unfolds between you. That said, it is completely fine for one partner to begin alone if the other is not ready yet or is unavailable for a session. Starting on your own can still bring helpful insight and often opens the door to working together later.

items.q: What can couples counselling help with?
items.a: Couples counselling can help with communication difficulties, emotional distance, recurring conflict, and rebuilding closeness and reconnection. It is also valuable during shared transitions such as relocation, new family stages, or navigating life across cultures and time zones. Whatever you are facing, the aim is to help you understand each other better and feel more like a team again.

Couples sessions usually run between 60 and 120 minutes, depending on what suits you and what you want to work on. The longer format can give a couple more room to explore a topic fully without feeling rushed. We can agree on the right length together, and it can be adjusted as we go.

items.q: Can we attend from different countries or time zones?
items.a: Yes. Because sessions take place online, the two of you can join from different locations or time zones and still meet together in the same virtual room. This works well for partners who travel, live apart for a time, or are relocating. I work across time zones by arrangement, based in Central European Time, so we can find a slot that works for you both.

items.q: Is couples counselling only for relationships in crisis?
items.a: No. Couples counselling is not only for relationships that are struggling. Many couples come to strengthen an already good relationship, deepen their connection, or navigate a shared transition together. It can be a caring, proactive way to invest in your relationship at any stage.
